URL: https://www.timesofisrael.com/eisenkot-edges-closer-to-government-as-his-party-announces-coalition-deal-with-democrats/
(Retrieved via WebFetch summary — full text not reproducible; Times of Israel's own reporting, 26 Nov 2026, Ariela Karmel, ToI Staff and Stav Levaton)

Yashar (Gadi Eisenkot) and The Democrats (Yair Golan) announced in a joint statement that they had agreed to sign a coalition deal, giving the Democrats four ministerial portfolios. This came two days after Golan froze talks over Yashar's unity talks with Likud. The portfolios are an expanded national security ministry, a merged labour and welfare ministry, communications, and culture and sports. The Democrats will also oversee the Social Equality Ministry. The Democrats did not get education or justice.
Itamar Ben Gvir, on the news: "terrorists are rejoicing, Jews are crying."
Ra'am chief Mansour Abbas predicted a government of the change bloc and UTJ, "with Ra'am's participation."
Naftali Bennett, on his Likud contacts: "The candle is still burning."

URL: https://www.timesofisrael.com/eisenkot-hopes-to-get-his-government-sworn-in-next-week-regardless-of-netanyahu-trial-drama/
(Tal Schneider, Times of Israel, 26 Nov 2026 — WebFetch summary)
Eisenkot has 10 days left to report a coalition to the president. His 28-day window ends Sunday, December 6, so his bloc prefers a swearing-in on Wednesday, December 2. Eisenkot will likely get a 14-day extension from President Herzog, to December 20. The judges' ruling in Netanyahu's trial did not change coalition dynamics.

URL: https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/eisenkot-golan-announce-coalition-deal-handing-democrats-4-ministerial-posts/
(Search snippet content — Times of Israel's own reporting language)
The party said the agreement includes a commitment to fully repeal the judicial overhaul. Yashar and its presumed partners hold 48 of the Knesset's 120 seats, still short of the 61 needed for a majority. Eisenkot is courting UTJ and Ra'am.
